sub_requests.narrative: Soft organic soil at gym footing F-12. Geotech had us over-ex and replace with structural fill. Price covers the dig, haul-off, fill and compaction testing support.

lines.desc: Structural fill, placed and compacted, 140 cy

sub_requests.narrative: RFI-112 came back adding two overflow drains on the gym roof. Our price covers the drain bodies, the leaders down to the storm tie-in and our plumber's time. No schedule impact if we get the go-ahead before the roofer closes up.

lines.desc: Overflow roof drain body and dome, 2 ea
4" cast iron leader and fittings, 86 lf

sub_requests.narrative: ASI-014 bumps eight corridor doors to 90-minute. That means new rated hardware and labels on all eight. ASI says no cost but the rated sets cost more than what we bought, so here's the difference.
RFI-171 adds strobes in the corridors. Devices, wire and programming. Our guys started on the 4th when the answer came out.
Closers for corridor doors C201 to C212 per RFI-175. Closers, templates and install.
District wants 24 more data drops in the library. We do the boxes, rings and conduit; Lakeside pulls and terminates the Cat 6. Their quote is attached with our 5 percent on it.

lines.desc: Box, ring, conduit per drop, 24 ea
Lower tier: Lakeside Low Voltage, Cat 6 cabling, termination, testing

sub_requests.narrative: ASI-040 seismic bracing for all mechanical systems. Big one. Bracing hardware, engineering and install crews across both wings and the addition.

lines.desc: Seismic bracing, ductwork and piping, 1 ls

sub_requests.narrative: ASI-040 seismic bracing on the electrical side: conduit racks, panels and lighting. Hardware plus labor.

lines.desc: Seismic bracing, conduit and equipment, 1 ls

sub_requests.narrative: RFI-180 moves the kitchen hood. Re-hang hood, extend the duct and rework the fire wrap.
Credit for deleting the bus loop walkway canopy. Steel was not fabricated yet so the full canopy package comes out, less what we already spent on shop drawings.
Submittal came back Approved as Noted calling for 18 gauge studs at the gym instead of 20. This is the material difference plus extra labor for the heavier stud.
Two added toilet partitions per ASI-044. Our subcontract allows 12 percent so that's what we carried.
T&M for the 14 access panels from RFI-131. All tags were signed by your super and the district rep each day. Totals below match the tags.
Gym sound panels per the district. Lump sum, supplied and installed.

lines.desc: Lump sum, supplied and installed (no breakdown)

sub_requests.narrative: District wants a stage lift in the multipurpose room so we need a pit. Dig, form, pour and waterproof after footings and before the slab. About 6 working days of our crew, and the slab can't go until it's done.

lines.desc: Pit walls and slab, formed and poured, 14 cy

sub_requests.narrative: Our crawler crane is tied up on another job and gets to you 5 working days late. Asking for the time and our standby while the crew waits.
RFI-214 changed the gym truss bearings. We have to field weld new slotted bearing assemblies after the trusses are set. Figure 4 working days of welding before deck can go on.
Fabric-wrapped panels in the music and band rooms per the district letter. This is our panels and install. The blocking from Ridgeline will come separately once they price it.
Supplement to our earlier request: Ridgeline's price for the wall blocking behind the music room panels, with our 5 percent.

lines.desc: Lower tier: Ridgeline Carpentry, In-wall blocking, rooms 205-206

sub_requests.narrative: Second play structure and surfacing at the primary playground per the district. Equipment, footings, surfacing and install.
ASI-061 flips the Wing A casework to the other walls. We add new blocking and patch the old locations.

lines.desc: Drywall patch at old locations, 9 room

sub_requests.narrative: Pricing for the two emergency gas shutoffs from RFI-183, same as my email. Valves with buttons, piping and plumber time.

lines.desc: Emergency gas shutoff valve with button, 2 ea
